title: Add Dual Quaternion Skinning to Mesh Instances

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: An implementation of https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9235. Alternative to the older implementation #89131. ## For Reviewers: I didn't bother doing 2D mesh/skeleton skinning, but with some encouragement and pointers on what needs to be done, I think I could do it. I'm also not sure I handled the GLES3 shader correctly at all. It's a bit more complicated than the Forward+ was. ## Details: This implementation is a variation of the source found (here)[https://users.cs.utah.edu/~ladislav/dq/index.html]. I properly attributed the original source in the shader code wherever I could. This doesn't actually change the CPU side bone transformation matrices either in mesh storage or the compute shader buffers. Instead, this merely adds a new parameter uniform enumeration to decide which style of skinning is used. The default path is to use traditional linear blend skinning. I added 2 other methods, both variants of Dual Quaternion. The first method is traditional dual quaternion skinning where all the scale/shear in the original bone transforms is lost. There is technically an opportunity to reduce the bone transform storage and transfer sizes from 12 floats to 8, but I didn't modify that part of the pipeline. The other version of dual quaternion skinning I added is a "scaled" dual quaternion which applies both dual quaternion skinning and the pure non-orthonormal part of the linear blend matrix to the final matrix. RenderingServer now has a new enumeration MeshSkinningMethod with 3 values (for now). That is set by the method "instance_set_skinning_method" for each mesh instance. MeshInstance3D also duplicates the enumeration definition from RenderingServer with its own setters/getters. ## Reference Test Project: [dual-quaternion-skinning.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32590699/dual-quaternion-skinning.zip) This is a humanoid character that was made in Blender with "preserve volume" enabled to help keep certain... assets... from candy-striping while posing. There are a few animations to test out the skinning. Especially useful is the "crouch" animation since it deforms the lower torso and thigh areas quite a bit under LBS. There is also some bone scaling thrown in to shakedown whether the scaling is applied correctly in conjunction with QDS. See attached screenshots for some comparisons: ## Future work / chances for improvement: There could be some kind of pipeline that lets you set the skinning method per-bone, but I didn't go that deep for this implementation. I just copied the same logic as Blender's "preserver volume" option for armature modifiers. Other skinning methods such as DIRECT_DELTA_MUSH could be added in the future, along with some other sophisticated methods I may have never heard of. * *Bugsquad edit, closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9235*
